nodes.name: One-step electrodeposition of RMNCL
nodes.procedure: First, 10 mmol Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 10 mmol Ni(CH₃COO)₂·4H₂O, 1.8 mmol RuCl₃, and 1.2 mmol MnCl₂·4H₂O were dissolved in 60 mL of deionized water. The solution was mixed using a magnetic stirrer and ultrasonication to homogenize it. The homogenized solution was then transferred into an electrolytic cell. Electrodeposition was carried out utilizing a standard three-electrode system. A carbon cloth (2×2 cm) was soaked under the liquid as the working electrode. The reference electrode used was the saturated calomel electrode (SCE), while the counter electrode was a carbon rod. The samples were subjected to cyclic voltammetry, with a potential scan of 0 to -1.8 V vs. SCE, scanning rate of 50 mV s⁻¹, and 40 scanning cycles. The resulting samples were washed with anhydrous ethanol and deionized water, then dried in a vacuum drying oven.

nodes.name: Phosphorization of RMNCL to RMNCP
nodes.procedure: The prepared precursor [RMNCL] and NaH₂PO₂·H₂O (2 g) were placed in the center and upstream side of the tube furnace, respectively. They were heated to 350°C under an argon atmosphere at a ramp rate of 2°C/min and held for two hours to synthesize the phosphide nanoflowers. Once cooled, the samples were removed.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCL, RMNCP, RNCP, and NCP show interconnected nanosheet/nanoflower morphology on carbon cloth, retained after phosphatization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images (Fig. 1c, S4 and S5) of the prepared RMNCP, Ru doped NiCoP (RNCP) and NiCoP (NCP) demonstrate that the interconnected nanosheet configuration are effectively retained, and the thickness of the nanoflower increases.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP exhibits nanosheet structure with lattice spacings of 0.351 nm (001 plane) and 0.242 nm (111 plane). Lattice spacing increases after Ru and Mn co-doping compared to undoped NiCoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was utilized to demonstrate the unique structure of the various samples. Fig. 1d also shows that RMNCP has a nanosheet structure. Additionally, the RMNCP (Fig. 1e) exhibits lattice stripe spacings of 0.351 and 0.242 nm, which correspond to its (001) and (111) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP nanoflower structure from nanosheets confirmed by HAADF-STEM with uniform Ru, Mn, Ni, Co, P elemental distribution by EDS mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image shown in Fig. 1h also confirms that the synthesized RMNCP has a nanoflower structure assembled from nanosheets... corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) images display a uniform distribution of Ru, Mn, Ni, Co and P elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP shows valence band maximum Ev=4.72 eV (vs RNCP 4.65 eV, NCP 4.55 eV) and reduced work function due to Ru/Mn co-doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the valence band maximum (EV) of RMNCP is 4.72 eV, which is considerably higher than those of RNCP (4.65 eV) and NCP (4.55 eV)... co-doping results in a significant decrease in the catalyst's work function.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCL shows negatively shifted Co and Ni binding energies compared to NCL. RMNCP shows Ruδ+ state, Mn2+/3+/4+ coexistence (641.77, 644.00, 646.70 eV), negative shifts in Ni/Co peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Next, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was used to probe the surface chemical composition... the Co and Ni species in RMNCL display negatively shifted binding energies when compared to NCL... The Mn 2p spectra (Fig. 2h) of RMNCP reveals the coexistence of Mn2+ (641.77 eV), Mn3+ (644.00 eV), and Mn4+ ions (646.70 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP corresponds to NiCoP phase (PDF#71-2336). RMNCL corresponds to NiCo LDH phase (PDF#40-0216).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis (Fig. S17) shows that RMNCP corresponds well to the NiCoP phase (PDF#71-2336) and RMNCL corresponds well to the NiCo LDH phase (PDF#40-0216).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge of RMNCP between Co foil and CoO (valence 0 to +2). Ru K-edge shows slight positive valence Ruδ+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge XANES spectra (Fig. 3a) reveal that the Co K-edge is located between metallic Co foil and CoO... Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra (Fig. 3d) unveil distinctions in the Ru K-edge of RMNCP compared to Ru foil and RuO2, indicating a slight positive valence state of Ru (Ruδ+).

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP FT-EXAFS shows Co-P peak ~1.6Å, Co-Ni ~2.4Å; Ru-P peak ~1.7Å confirming dispersed Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectra (Fig. 3b) exhibit a distinct peak at ~1.6Å... suggesting association with Co-P... Ru-P bond can be ascribed to the distinct peak (~1.7Å) found in the FT-EXAFS spectrum of Ru...
